I went to a café (   ) meeting a friend.

Adding the restrictive “만” (only) to the causal “때문에” (because of) gives the meaning solely because of that. It does not express the intended purpose of meeting a friend here.
This marks a starting point in time or place. Here the sentence needs the purpose of going to the café, not a starting point.
This expresses similarity to something. It does not establish the purpose relationship between “친구를 만나기” (meeting a friend) and “카페에 가기” (going to a café).

【Why this is correct】“친구를 만나기” (meeting a friend) is the purpose of going to the café. The verb construction “-기 위해서” expresses the purpose of an action, so “친구를 만나기 위해서 카페에 갔습니다” means “I went to a café to meet a friend” and is natural here.
【Distractor traps】“부터” marks a starting point, and “처럼” expresses similarity or comparison. “때문에만” adds an exclusive only restriction to a cause, so it does not fit this sentence expressing the purpose of meeting someone.
【How to approach this question type】Look at what the action in the following clause is intended to achieve. Distinguish purpose, expressed with “V-기 위해서”, from the reason for doing something, expressed with forms such as “-기 때문에”.
In the current option order, choice 3 is correct.

fields.text: Choose the statement with the same meaning as the following.
I exercise alone every weekday.
I stopped by home before the meeting.
I play tennis with my younger sibling on Saturday or Sunday.
This shop does not sell fruit.
I play tennis with my younger sibling every weekend.
Choose the sentence with the same meaning.
“저는 평일마다 혼자 운동합니다.” (I exercise alone every weekday.) changes at least one of the original’s actor, action, time or causal relationships, so it does not mean the same thing.
“회의 전에 집에 들렀습니다.” (I stopped by home before the meeting.) changes at least one of the original’s actor, action, time or causal relationships, so it does not mean the same thing.
“이 가게는 과일을 팔지 않습니다.” (This shop does not sell fruit.) changes at least one of the original’s actor, action, time or causal relationships, so it does not mean the same thing.

【Why this is correct】The original “저는 주말마다 동생과 테니스를 칩니다.” (I play tennis with my younger sibling every weekend.) and “저는 토요일이나 일요일에 동생과 테니스를 합니다.” (I play tennis with my younger sibling on Saturday or Sunday.) have the same actor, action and time relationships; only the wording differs.
In the current option order, choice 3 is correct.
Choose the statement with the same meaning as the following.
I stopped by home before the meeting.
I finished the meeting and went home right away.
I exercise alone every weekday.
This shop does not sell fruit.
I went straight home after the meeting ended.
Choose the sentence with the same meaning.
“전에” means before the meeting, reversing the order in “끝난 후에” (after it ended). “들렀습니다” (stopped by) also differs from going straight home.
A weekday exercise habit differs in both subject matter and action from going home after a meeting.
Whether a shop sells fruit has nothing to do with going home after a meeting.

【Why this is correct】“회의가 끝난 후에 바로 집에 갔습니다” means going straight home after the meeting ended. “회의를 마치고 곧 집으로 갔습니다” has the same event order and action. The correct expression is “회의를 마치고 곧 집으로 갔습니다.” (I finished the meeting and went home right away).
【Distractor traps】The main trap reverses “후에(뒤에)” (after) into “전에(앞에)” (before). The exercise and fruit-selling options are unrelated to the meeting and return home.
【How to approach this question type】Briefly mark the actor, action and time order. Here, keep only an option preserving both meeting ends → immediate return home.
In the current option order, choice 2 is correct.
